newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor hikes power rates in most grids.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor hikes power rates in most grids.

text.p: The state-run National Power Corp announced on Monday a power rate cut in two grids in the Philippines but said it raised rates in three others.
In a statement, Napocor said it reduced power rates in the main northern island of Luzon by 1.29 centavos per kilowatt-hour (kwh) due to lower bunker and diesel fuel cost.
The power firm said it also cut rates in the Cebu-Panay-Negros grids in central Philippines by 3.47 centavos.

Napocor said in the Bohol grid in the central Philippines it decided to raise rates by 1.08 centavos per kwh; in the central Leyte-Samar grid by 1.12 centavos and in the southern island of Mindanao by 0.31 centavos per kwh.
The price adjustments would take effect from April 26 to May 25.
The adjustments are part of the monthly automatic price changes made by the power firm to reflect fuel price movements and foreign exchange fluctuations.
The government plans to privatise Napocor, the biggest producer of power in the country, with the passage of a bill in Congress that would mandate its sale.
